subject: greatWyrm
kind: god body portrait (plan 3.1: whole body, regal pose, variant 0, swatch 0)
prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Great Wyrm, a colossal winged dragon-god, the monster of the age, in a regal pose: standing four-square on the ground, its long neck raised high in an S-curve so that its head is the highest point, chin lifted, jaws closed, the wings half raised and folded at the elbows behind its shoulders, its long tail curled forward around its feet. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the head about 6% from the top edge and the feet and tail about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the head, the horns, the neck and the wings that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the feet and tail.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the raised head, the horns, the wings and the tail against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the beast is its wing membranes: dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Nothing in the image glows: no fire, no smoke, the jaws are closed. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Body: a heavy four-legged dragon with two great wings, a long neck and a long tail; scales of bronze-brown (#8A6A3E) crossed by broad darker bands edged with lichen grey-green (#909080) along the flanks, the neck and the tail; a paler bronze belly of broad plates; strong clawed feet. Head: a long wedge-shaped head with a heavy jaw, the jaws closed, dark amber eyes. Horns: two long smooth horns swept straight back from the brow along the line of the neck; no other horns, no frill, no crown of spines. Wings: smooth, unbroken wing membranes, whole to their trailing edges, with no tears, no holes, no ragged or tattered edges and no ribs showing through, of dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour, darker toward their edges, stretched between dark bronze wing bones. Tail: a long tail ending in a flat spade-shaped tip.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view; a little more weathered and ancient in its surfaces, with a heavier, more imposing stance.
